declared.title: There Are Plenty of Fish in the Sea: The Effects of Choice Overload and Reversibility on Online Daters’ Satisfaction With Selected Partners
declared.foundIn: recherche OpenAlex « reversible decisions satisfaction » du 2026-11-22 (dossier too-many-choices) ; titre relevé sur OpenAlex : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: online daters choosing a partner from 6 or 24 profiles, reversible or not, followed one week (authors in the US); sample size not given in the abstract

findings.text: A week after choosing from 24 profiles rather than 6, daters were less satisfied with their choice and more likely to change it

support.sentence: Drawing on the choice overload and decision reversibility theoretical frameworks, we show that, a week after making their selection, online daters who chose from a large set of potential partners (i.e., 24) were less satisfied with their choice than those who selected from a small set (i.e., 6), and were more likely to change their selection.

findings.text: Being able to reverse the choice did not lower satisfaction by itself; only daters with a large pool and a reversible choice were the least satisfied

support.sentence: While choice reversibility did not affect daters' satisfaction, those who selected from a large pool and had the ability to reverse their choice were the least satisfied with their selected partner after one week.

limits: a partner chosen from profiles in a study, not a real relationship
sample size not given in the abstract
